docs.title: keelyard
docs.text:
Your coding agent has to show its work before it can say "done". Every edit is snapshotted, so any step can be undone. Logs are trimmed before they eat the context window. keelyard works with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

pipx install keelyard
cd your-project
keelyard init

That is the whole setup. keelyard init finds the agents on your machine and wires each one: hooks, the MCP server, a short guide in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md, and a skill plus slash commands for Claude Code. After that it takes a first snapshot.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text: What you get Proof gate The agent can't finish until there is a checklist, evidence for every item, and a passing test run after its last edit. You get a one-file HTML report. Rewind A snapshot after every edit, in a separate git repo. Undo any step and fork from any step. Smaller context Output filters that keep every failure, deduplicated reads, project_map / outline / find_symbol. Memory and usage Search across past sessions from all three agents. Tokens and cost from local logs. Swarm Bulk reading and drafting on a cheap model, with every citation checked. Arena One task, several agents and models: pass rate, time and tokens side by side.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text: keelyard is not a proxy and does not read your API traffic. It does not change your .git, and it does not send anything over the network unless you configure a helper model for swarm. Every number in these docs was measured. See Benchmarks, including the results that did not go our way.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
Rerun them yourself

make bench (offline, $0) and make codex-e2e reproduce these numbers and the Codex check. Commands and methodology: BENCHMARKS.md in the repo.

Machine: 8 vCPU Linux box, no GPU, Python 3.13. Measured on 2026-10-12. Token counts are chars / 4.

docs.title: Terse-output rule, measured on local models (Oct 17, 2026)
docs.text:
python bench/terse.py --models qwen2.5-0.5b,llama3.2-1b,qwen-coder-1.5b --seeds 1,2 (Ollama, Q4, temperature 0.3): 32 coding prompts x 2 seeds = 64 answers per model and rule. Tokens are Ollama's own counts, input (prompt_eval_count, so the rule's cost is included) + output (eval_count). "Facts" = the answer contains what the prompt needs (identifier, fix, error name). Raw numbers: bench/terse.json. $0, no paid calls.

rule total tokens (3 models) facts (of 192) old "Be terse: no preamble, no restating the question, no summary of what you are about to do." 24,053 142 previous rule ("Reply with results only: ... exact and complete.", ~33 tokens) 31,870 150 shipped: "Be terse: no preamble or recap. Keep code exact." (~12 tokens) 23,428 (−2.6% vs old) 155 "Be terse. Keep code and facts." 27,310 158 "Be terse: answer first, no preamble or recap; keep code and facts complete." 28,827 155

Per model (total / facts): qwen2.5-0.5b old 9,444/44, shipped 8,271/45; llama3.2-1b old 6,884/45, previous 10,799/52, shipped 7,022/49; qwen-coder-1.5b old 7,725/53, previous 12,342/51, shipped 8,135/61.

  • The shipped rule beats the old line on total tokens and the previous rule on facts summed over three models, but not on every model: on llama3.2-1b it uses 2% more tokens than the old line and keeps fewer facts than the previous rule. The token margin over the old line is small. Not measured with Claude or GPT models.
  • Lossless JSON compaction: pretty gh search repos --json output 2,121 → 1,236 tokens (−42%), decoded back exactly (bench/mechanisms.py). An already-minified GitHub issue list shrank only 3%.
  • The repeated-failure hint (about 40 tokens, only when it fires) was not measured for savings.

docs.title: Token-saving mechanisms, measured locally (Oct 16, 2026)
docs.text:
python bench/mechanisms.py (no model, no network, $0). Tokens are chars / 4. Fixtures: this repo, the installed httpx package source, and the two-file examples/arena/discount/repo. The keelyard row shifts a little with every commit (it measures itself). Each row compares keelyard with what an agent does without it, and checks the agent still gets what it needs. Raw numbers: bench/mechanisms.json.

mechanism baseline keelyard keelyard repo httpx discount (2 files) correctness check 1 find code grep the name, read the whole defining file ranked find_symbol page + outline + the definition's lines + related 16,969 → 3,691 (−78%) 54,731 → 16,717 (−69%) 107 → 108 (+1%) the definition is in the slice read 2 re-reads read, re-read, read after a 1-line edit (5 largest files) full, "unchanged" notice, diff 127,392 → 43,289 (−66%) 146,937 → 49,689 (−66%) 456 → 387 (−15%) diff applied to the first read = the edited file; force=true returns all of it 3 logs, real pytest -v raw output filter_output 1,233 → 9 (all passed) – 401 → 149 (−63%, 2 failures) every error/failure/count line kept; failing test ids kept 3 logs, corpus (10 tools, pytest padded with 300 passes) raw filtered 7,965 → 1,502 (−81%) same 4 paging every match in one response first page of 20 + remaining/next_offset 8,849 → 416 (−95%) 7,007 → 324 (−95%) 99 → 99 (0%) walking every page returns every result in order 5 work state re-read the 3 changed files after a compaction (modeled) work_state render 26,574 → 241 33,055 → 182 177 → 111 every ref resolves to a real file line or command 6 tool schemas per request core (14 tools) lazy (6 tools) 2,319 → 927 (−60%) every hidden core tool is found by tool_search

What this does not show: - Row 1 on a tiny repo is one token worse: when the file is smaller than an outline, just read it. - Row 4 saves only when the answer is on the first page; reading every page costs slightly more than one dump. - Row 5's baseline is a model of what an agent re-reads, not a measured session. - Row 6: each on-demand tool use (search + call) adds about 309 tokens that stay in context, so lazy is smaller only while a session uses fewer than 4 distinct hidden tools. The proof workflow alone uses about 4, which is why core stays the default and lazy is opt-in. - None of this was measured in a live agent session.

docs.title: Head-to-head with rtk (bench/vs_rtk.py)
docs.text:
gh release download -R rtk-ai/rtk -p 'rtk-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz' && tar xzf rtk-*.tar.gz
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/django/django /tmp/djb
git clone --depth 80 https://github.com/psf/requests /tmp/req
python bench/vs_rtk.py --rtk ./rtk --django /tmp/djb --history /tmp/req --json bench/vs_rtk_results.json
python bench/plot_vs_rtk.py

The script builds scratch repos: a Django clone with 5 edited files, 3 untracked and 1 deleted; a pytest project with 4 failing tests out of 125; and a Rust crate with 2 failing tests out of 42. It runs each command once and feeds the same raw output to keelyard, while rtk runs the command itself. FORCE_COLOR is removed and NO_COLOR=1 is set for all runs. "Facts" are extracted from the raw output with fixed rules (see facts_* in the script) and count as kept when every part appears verbatim in the filtered text.

command facts raw tok keelyard tok keelyard kept rtk tok rtk kept git status 9 161 61 100% 58 100% git log -n 40 (requests) 40 6,807 950 100% 2,378 100% git diff 91 1,653 1,064 100% 1,557 100% grep -rn (django) 15 277 230 100% 277 100% find *.py (admin) 30 299 136 100% 113 100% ruff check (django/utils) 307 43,582 3,022 100% 1,050 24% pytest -v (4 failing of 125) 7 3,289 312 100% 195 71% cargo test (2 failing of 42) 6 454 126 100% 119 100% total 56,522 5,901 5,747

Caveats: one run per command, eight commands, fact rules written by us. rtk drops line numbers from ruff results and some assertion lines from pytest, which is why its retention is lower on those two. rtk handles many more tools.

docs.title: Swarm with a small local model
docs.text:
These are real calls to qwen2.5-coder-1.5b-instruct (Q4_K_M GGUF) served by Ollama on CPU, with concurrency 4. There were 12 tasks against this repo: 8 Q&A or summaries, 2 patch drafts and 2 greps.

  • Wall time: 4 min 15 s; helper tokens: 14,452 in, 1,409 out.
  • Verified: 3/12. Both greps are local and need no model. One patch passed git apply --check; the other did not apply.
  • Q&A: 0/8 answers contained a valid path:line citation, and the verifier marked all 8 UNVERIFIED. A second run with a format example in the prompt also verified 0/8. One answer copied the example's file name, so the example was removed again.

Conclusion: the verification layer does its job, but a 1.5B model is not a useful helper. Use a 7B+ local model or a hosted cheap model. We have not yet measured how well larger models verify.

docs.title: Swarm quality
docs.text:
python bench/swarm_quality.py --runs 2, local qwen-coder 1.5B on Ollama, 2026-10-12. Five one-function bug fixes and five "which line does X" questions, in a repo where each file also carries 25 unrelated helpers. Single is the old swarm: whole file, one sample, diff output, git apply --check only. Pipeline is the new one: context pack, one-definition rewrite, tests on a copy, best-of-3, one retry with feedback, no escalation (no strong model configured). Ground truth for fixes is that module's own tests passing with the patch; for questions, citing the expected line.

single, run 1 / 2 pipeline, run 1 / 2 fixes actually correct 0 / 0 of 5 4 / 4 of 5 fixes marked verified but wrong 3 / 2 0 / 0 questions citing the right line 1 / 1 of 5 2 / 3 of 5 questions marked verified 1 / 1 5 / 5 model calls 10 / 10 33 / 39 input tokens 12,435 / 12,435 5,034 / 6,309 output tokens 1,679 / 1,712 2,835 / 3,626

Checking patches against tests removed every false "verified" fix, and the rewrite format plus retries took a 1.5B model from 0 to 4 correct fixes out of 5. Context packs used about half the input tokens despite 3-4x more calls. What it does not show: a "verified" answer to a question means its citations exist, not that it is right (5 verified, 2-3 right). Ten tasks on one tiny model is a smoke test, not a benchmark; escalation and 7B+ models are not measured here.

docs.title: Cooperative swarm vs the best local setup
docs.text:
Same 10 tasks (5 bug fixes, 5 questions), qwen-coder-1.5b on Ollama, 2 runs each. python bench/swarm_quality.py.

mode correct of 20 (2 runs × 10) tokens tokens per correct wrong patches marked verified single 2 27,394 13,697 5 pipeline 15 19,073 1,272 0 best-local 18 28,081 1,560 0 coop-nocritic 15 19,686 1,312 0 coop 15 44,149 2,943 0
  • best-local is the same model with more samples and retries (best_of 5, retries 2). It stands in for "one strong agent" because no stronger model or API key was available. That comparison is still open.
  • coop adds the critic. It doubled the tokens and did not improve quality, so critic is off by default.
  • coop-nocritic (blackboard, voting, budget) costs about the same as the pipeline per correct answer. With one model the ladder had one step, so routing was not exercised here (it is covered by tests).

docs.title: keelyard's own overhead
docs.text:
python bench/overhead.py counts what keelyard adds to every session (characters / 4 of compact JSON or text):

item tokens MCP tool schemas, 13 core tools (default) 1,582 MCP tool schemas, all 22 tools ([mcp] tools = "all") 2,401 MCP server instructions 77 CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md guide block 144 session brief, fresh project (cap 600) 74 total per session, fresh project 1,877 workflow guide, only when asked (plan / debug / review) 240 / 181 / 182

Prompt recall adds at most 250 tokens per prompt and only when past sessions match; hints are capped at 12 per session.

Net: the 8 filtered commands above saved 50,621 tokens, so one session that runs them nets 48,744 tokens. At the median saving per command, the fixed overhead is repaid after 4 filtered commands. A session that never runs a noisy command pays the 1,877 tokens and saves nothing; these are per-command measurements, not totals from real sessions.

docs.title: keelyard alternatives and comparisons
docs.text: What other tools do, and when you might want them instead of, or next to, keelyard. Facts about other projects come from their own READMEs; numbers are only ours where we say "measured". Full table: Landscape.

docs.title: Built-in agent features
docs.text: need built into the agent what keelyard adds Undo an edit Claude Code has /rewind checkpoints and OpenCode has /undo, each for edits made in its own sessions snapshots after every edit and shell command, across all three agents, in a separate git dir; rewind is itself undoable Run tests every agent can run tests when it decides to a Stop hook that blocks finishing until a passing run after the last edit is recorded, and keeps the proof open if tests were weakened Project rules CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md a short block in those files plus hooks, so the rule is enforced, not only stated

docs.title: Output and context tools
docs.text:
• rtk: per-command output filters. On our 8 test commands we measured 56,522 → 5,747 tokens for rtk and 5,901 for keelyard. Use rtk if you only want output filtering.
  • repomix, code2prompt: pack a repository into one prompt. Good for one-shot chats; keelyard instead gives the agent ranked slices (find_symbol, outlines) during a session.
  • serena: symbol-level navigation and editing over LSP. Deeper code intelligence than keelyard's find_symbol.
  • ccusage: usage reports from local logs. keelyard's usage does a similar job across Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

docs.title: Workflow packs
docs.text: • superpowers, spec-kit: skills and spec-to-task workflows. keelyard ships small plan / review / debug commands, but its focus is enforcing proof, not planning.

docs.title: When keelyard is not the right tool
docs.text:
• You need a sandbox. keelyard runs as your user and is not a security boundary (Guarantees).
  • Your project has no tests. The proof gate can only check what your test suite checks.
  • You need to undo database changes, deployments or pushed commits. Snapshots hold files only.

docs.title: keelyard + Claude Code in 2 minutes
docs.text:
keelyard plugs into Claude Code through three things Claude Code already supports: lifecycle hooks (.claude/settings.json), an MCP server (.mcp.json), and CLAUDE.md. You keep using Claude Code as usual.

Checked with Claude Code 2.1.197 (Oct 29, 2026) by scripts/claude_e2e.py: the real claude binary in -p mode against a local scripted model (ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL), so no Anthropic key is used. CI runs it on every push and weekly.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pipx install keelyard                       # or: pip install keelyard
npm i -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code          # if you don't have Claude Code yet

docs.title: 2. Wire up your project
docs.text:
cd your-project
keelyard init --agent claude
keelyard doctor

This writes:

File What it holds .claude/settings.json hooks SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop → keelyard hook claude <event>; lean preset also sets env (capped tool output, no extra model calls) .mcp.json mcpServers.keelyard → keelyard mcp (project scope) CLAUDE.md a short block between <!-- keelyard:start --> and <!-- keelyard:end --> .claude/skills/keelyard/ a keelyard skill .claude/commands/keelyard/ /keelyard:prove, review, status, debug, plan, undo .keelyard/ config and snapshots (a separate git dir; your .git is never touched)

Originals are kept, and keelyard uninstall claude restores them. For every project at once, use keelyard init --global (writes ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude.json and ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md).

docs.title: 3. Approve the MCP server once
docs.text:
Claude Code asks before it starts servers from a project's .mcp.json. Until then:

$ claude mcp list
keelyard: keelyard mcp - ⏸ Pending approval (run `claude` to approve)

Start claude in the project and accept the keelyard server. Prefer it for every project? Run claude mcp add --scope user keelyard -- keelyard mcp instead. The hooks need no approval.

docs.title: 4. What you see
docs.text:
• Session start: a brief with the project's test command and a baseline test result.
  • Every edit (Edit/Write or a Bash command that changes files) is snapshotted: keelyard rewind list, keelyard rewind to 3.
  • When Claude says "done" with red or unrun tests, the Stop hook sends it back:
Stop hook feedback:
keelyard proof gate: you changed files but have not proven the work yet.

A test run in Claude's own Bash tool counts as proof. The gate gives up after three blocks, so it never loops. - Tools: mcp__keelyard__proof_check, proof_run_tests, memory_search, find_symbol, … are available to the model. - Afterwards: keelyard status shows proof proven, the evidence and the timeline.

docs.title: What was checked (Claude Code 2.1.197)
docs.text:
Check Result claude mcp list shows keelyard from .mcp.json yes (pending approval until accepted) keelyard MCP tools and the CLAUDE.md block reach the model yes hooks fire: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop yes (PreCompact needs a long session) gate blocks a "Done." after a breaking edit with no test run yes gate opens after a passing pytest in Claude's Bash yes, keelyard status → proven keelyard rewind to 2 brings back the broken edit yes

Not checked: token savings with a real Claude model, and PreCompact (needs a long session).

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
Generated from keelyard --help by docs/demo/gen_reference.py.

Every command accepts --json and prints exactly one JSON object with ok and exit keys.

usage: keelyard <command> [options]

keelyard makes coding agents prove their work, lets you undo any step,
and keeps their context small. Works with Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode.

start here:
  init              set up this project and wire every agent it finds
  doctor            check that everything is installed and wired correctly
  status            what keelyard knows about this project right now

everyday:
  rewind            list, inspect and undo agent steps
  proof             the evidence an agent collected before saying "done"
  run               run a command and print a compact version of its output
  code              outline a file, map the project, find a symbol
  memory            search past sessions across all your agents
  usage             tokens and cost from your local agent logs

more:
  swarm             fan small, checkable tasks out to a cheap model
  arena             run one task across agents and models, compare results
  bench             measure savings on your own machine
  selftest          a scripted agent completes a full task through the agent interface
  install/uninstall wire or unwire one agent by hand
  filter            compact output piped on stdin
  recall            print the full output that `run` shortened

options:
  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
  --version    show program's version number and exit

commands:
  <command>
    init       set up this project and wire the agents found on this machine
    doctor     check the installation and wiring; exits 3 if something is broken
    status     show what keelyard knows about this project
    selftest   a scripted agent runs a full task through MCP and hooks in a temp folder
    install    wire one agent in this project
    uninstall  unwire one agent in this project
    rewind     list, inspect and undo agent steps
    proof      the evidence an agent collected before saying done
    run        run a command and print a compact version of its output
    filter     compact output piped on stdin
    recall     print the full output that `run` shortened
    code       outline a file, map the project, find a symbol
    memory     search past sessions across all your agents
    state      compact work state: requirements, decisions, changes, open questions
    usage      tokens and cost from your local agent logs
    swarm      fan small, checkable tasks out to a cheap model
    arena      run one task across agents and models, compare results
    bench      measure savings on your own machine

exit codes:
  0  success
  1  error (the message says what went wrong and how to fix it)
  2  usage error (bad command or arguments)
  3  a check did not pass (doctor found a problem, proof not complete, tests failed, selftest failed)
  `keelyard run` exits with the code of the command it ran.

Run `keelyard <command> --help` for examples. Every command accepts --json.

docs.text:
usage: keelyard init [-h] [--json] [--agent {claude,codex,opencode}] [--no-agents] [--dry-run]
                     [--preset {lean,balanced,max-quality}] [--codex-project-mcp] [--no-terse]
                     [--global]

set up this project and wire the agents found on this machine

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --json                print one JSON object on stdout (for scripts and agents)

docs.title: keelyard + Codex in 2 minutes
docs.text:
keelyard plugs into the Codex CLI through three things Codex already supports: lifecycle hooks (.codex/hooks.json), an MCP server, and AGENTS.md. You keep using Codex as usual.

Checked with Codex CLI 0.165.0 (Oct 28, 2026) by scripts/codex_e2e.py, which runs the real Codex binary against a local scripted model, so it needs no OpenAI key. CI runs it on every push.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
pipx install keelyard        # or: pip install keelyard
npm i -g @openai/codex       # if you don't have Codex yet

docs.title: 2. Wire up your project
docs.text:
cd your-project
keelyard init --agent codex --codex-project-mcp
keelyard doctor

This writes:

File What it holds .codex/hooks.json SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop → keelyard hook codex <event> .codex/config.toml [mcp_servers.keelyard] (only with --codex-project-mcp) AGENTS.md a short block between <!-- keelyard:start --> and <!-- keelyard:end --> .keelyard/ config and snapshots (a separate git dir; your .git is never touched)

Originals are kept, and keelyard uninstall codex restores them byte for byte.

Prefer the MCP server for every project? Put it in ~/.codex/config.toml instead (or run codex mcp add keelyard -- keelyard mcp):

[mcp_servers.keelyard]
command = "keelyard"
args = ["mcp"]

codex mcp list should now show keelyard … enabled.

The AGENTS.md block keelyard adds (lean preset) is three lines:

## keelyard

Every edit is snapshotted (undo: `keelyard rewind list`, `keelyard rewind to N`). Your shell test runs are the proof:
run the project's tests after your last edit before you finish.
Be terse: no preamble or recap. Keep code exact.

docs.title: 3. Trust the hooks once
docs.text: Codex only runs hooks you have reviewed. Start codex in the project, type /hooks, and trust the five keelyard hooks. Codex also needs the project itself to be trusted to load .codex/ (it asks the first time). For one-off automation where you vetted the hooks yourself, codex exec --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust skips the review for that run.

docs.title: 4. What you see
docs.text:
• Session start: a brief with the project's test command and a baseline test result.
  • Every edit (apply_patch or a shell command that changes files) is snapshotted: keelyard rewind list, keelyard rewind to 3.
  • When Codex says "done" with red or unrun tests, the Stop hook sends it back with what is missing:
keelyard proof gate: you changed files but have not proven the work yet.
- No test run after the last edit (proof_run_tests phase='after', or `keelyard proof test after`).
Run the project's tests in your shell (that counts as proof), or use the keelyard proof tools, then finish.

A test run in Codex's own shell counts as proof; Codex does not need to call keelyard. The gate gives up after three blocks so a session can never loop forever. - Afterwards: keelyard status shows proof proven, the evidence and the timeline.

docs.title: Verify it yourself
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/akobirjontulqinovfuture/keelyard && cd keelyard
pip install -e . pytest && npm i -g @openai/codex
python scripts/codex_e2e.py

Expected output: 11 PASS lines (hooks file, AGENTS.md, codex mcp list, MCP tools and AGENTS.md reaching the model, each hook event firing, the gate blocking a red "Done.", the gate opening after a passing run, keelyard status proven, rewind restoring the broken edit).

docs.title: Known limits with Codex
docs.text:
• Output filtering does not apply. Codex hooks can't replace a shell result yet, so keelyard's log compression works through the MCP run_compact tool only, not on Codex's own shell calls.
  • No lean switch for Codex tools. The lean preset can turn some Claude Code / OpenCode tools off; Codex has no config for that, so on Codex lean means the shorter brief and AGENTS.md block.
  • Token savings on Codex are not measured yet. The e2e check uses a scripted model, which proves the wiring, not savings. Real-model numbers are on the roadmap.
  • Codex's own sandbox rejects some commands (for example rm -rf) before keelyard's PreToolUse sees them.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
keelyard init writes .keelyard/config.toml. Every field is optional. This is the default file:

# keelyard configuration. Every field is optional.

[proof]
# Block the agent from finishing until a proof bundle exists.
gate = true
# Command used for before/after test runs. Empty = auto-detect.
test_cmd = ""
# URL of the running app; when set, a screenshot is required for proof.
app_url = ""
# Stop the gate from looping forever: give up after this many blocks per session.
max_blocks = 3

[rewind]
enabled = true
# Files larger than this are left out of snapshots and listed as skipped.
max_file_mb = 20
# Tools that trigger a snapshot after they run.
snapshot_tools = ["Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit", "Bash", "apply_patch", "write", "edit", "bash", "patch"]

[swarm]
# Max concurrent helper calls.
concurrency = 16
# Hard cap on tasks per swarm call.
max_tasks = 256
# Which [models.*] entry helpers use.
helper_model = "cheap"
# Samples per task (best-of-N), retries with verifier feedback, and the model tried once when all fail
# ("" = no escalation). Draft patches are also run against the tests in a temporary copy.
best_of = 2
retries = 1
escalate_model = "strong"
test_patches = true
# Cooperative mode (default; `keelyard swarm run --basic` turns it off for one run): models tried cheapest first
# ([] = helper_model then escalate_model), concurrent workers, a peer critic, and hard token caps
# (0 = no cap). Calls are refused before they are made once a cap would be crossed.
cooperative = true
ladder = []
workers = 64
critic = false
budget_tokens = 200000
task_budget_tokens = 20000

[mcp]
# Tools the MCP server offers. Every schema costs tokens in every session, so the default is the 14 the
# workflow needs. "all" adds outline, project_map, rewind_diff, usage_report, route_task, swarm_plan,
# swarm_verify, status (and proof_screenshot, which "core" adds by itself when [proof].app_url is set).
# "lazy" sends only read_file, run_compact, find_symbol, proof_status plus tool_search/tool_call (about 60%
# fewer schema tokens than "core"); every other tool is found and run on demand. It falls back to "core"
# by itself if it would not be smaller.
tools = "core"

[saver]
# Deny a repeat Read of an unchanged file (reset on context compaction).
dedupe_reads = true
# Filter large Bash results before the model reads them (raw output kept for `keelyard recall`).
filter_bash = true
filter_min_chars = 1200
# Max characters returned by compress_output before head/tail trimming.
max_output_chars = 6000

# Optional prices for `keelyard usage`, USD per million tokens. keelyard ships none.
# [prices."your-model-name"]
# input = 0.0
# output = 0.0
# cache_read = 0.0
# cache_write = 0.0

# Models are plain names you choose; keelyard never assumes a vendor's lineup.
# provider = "openai" (any OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions) or "anthropic".
[models.cheap]
provider = "openai"
base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
api_key_env = ""

[models.strong]
provider = "anthropic"
base_url = "https://api.anthropic.com"
model = "set-me"
api_key_env = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"

.keelyard/ also holds snapshots (shadow.git, steps.jsonl), proof bundles, shortened outputs (raw/) and the hook error log (hook.log). The folder contains a .gitignore with *, so it is never committed.

Environment variables:

variable effect KEELYARD_ROOT use this folder as the project root instead of searching upward for .keelyard or .git XDG_DATA_HOME where the memory index lives (default ~/.local/share/keelyard) NO_COLOR, FORCE_COLOR=0 plain terminal output

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Short answers to the questions people ask about keelyard. Every claim links to the page with the details.

docs.title: What is keelyard?
docs.text: keelyard is an open-source (Apache-2.0) command-line tool and MCP server that makes AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode) prove their work with a passing test run before they can finish, snapshots every edit so any step can be undone, and trims noisy tool output. It runs locally, with no telemetry.

docs.title: How do I make Claude Code or Codex prove the tests pass before it says "done"?
docs.text:
Install keelyard and wire it into the project:

pipx install keelyard
keelyard init --agent claude     # or: --agent codex

This adds a Stop hook. When the agent changed files and tries to finish without a passing test run after its last edit, the hook blocks it and says what is missing. A test run in the agent's own shell counts as proof. See Proof gate, Claude Code in 2 minutes and Codex in 2 minutes.

docs.title: Can the agent cheat by deleting or weakening tests?
docs.text: keelyard keeps the proof open when tests are deleted, when there are fewer test functions or assertions, when new skip/xfail/only markers appear, or when fewer tests run than before. It does not catch every weakening: changing an expected value still looks fine. Details: Guarantees and limits.

docs.title: How do I roll back a bad step an AI coding agent made?
docs.text:
keelyard snapshots the project after every edit and shell command, in a separate git directory (.keelyard/shadow.git), so your own .git is never touched.

keelyard rewind list
keelyard rewind to 3

A rewind first snapshots the current state, so it can be undone too. Snapshots hold files only: databases, pushed commits and package installs are not restored. See Rewind.

docs.title: How do I reduce the tokens a coding agent uses?
docs.text: keelyard's lean preset (the default for init) caps tool output, filters noisy logs (test runners, git, package managers) and gives the agent smaller code views. On our own benchmark of six tasks run in OpenCode (3–8 runs per setup), whole-session tokens went from 267,525 to 52,745 (−80%) with equal or better correctness. That is one benchmark on one agent with small samples; savings on Claude Code and Codex are not measured yet. See Benchmarks and Presets.

docs.title: Does it need an API key or send my code anywhere?
docs.text: No. keelyard runs on your machine and makes no network calls, except to model endpoints you configure yourself for the optional swarm and coop commands. The end-to-end checks in CI use a local scripted model, so they need no key either.

docs.title: Which agents and platforms are supported?
docs.text: Claude Code, Codex CLI and OpenCode, on Linux, macOS and Windows, with Python 3.11+. Claude Code and Codex are checked end to end in CI on every push with the real CLIs. See For agents.

docs.title: How is keelyard different from other tools?
docs.text: Most related tools do one thing: shrink output, pack the repo, or track usage. keelyard's main job is the proof gate plus undo, with output trimming as a side benefit. See Alternatives.

docs.title: How do I remove it?
docs.text: keelyard uninstall claude (or codex, opencode) restores the files init changed. keelyard uninstall --global does the same for user-level config.

docs.title: What keelyard guarantees, and what it doesn't
docs.text: keelyard is a local tool that runs as you. It makes an agent's claims checkable and its file edits undoable. It is not a sandbox. This page lists exactly what holds and where the limits are.

docs.title: Proof
docs.text: keelyard guarantees it does not guarantee "proven" means a passing test run was recorded for the current file contents. Any change to a snapshotted file after that run (even one made without a hook firing) reopens the proof. That your tests are good. A proof is only as strong as the test suite. Evidence is shown at three levels, never merged: test-verified (keelyard ran the test command itself), command-succeeded (the agent ran tests in its shell and the agent harness reported the result), agent-claimed (the agent wrote it, e.g. a checklist tick or accept-tests). That agent-claimed evidence is true. It is shown so you can judge it. Proof bundles are signed with a key kept outside the project (<data home>/keelyard/proof.key, mode 600). A bundle edited by hand, or with its signature removed, is never reported as proven again in that session. Protection against a process that deliberately reads that key. Anything running as your user can. Signing stops casual forging, not a determined attacker. Weakened tests keep the proof open: deleted test files, fewer test functions or assertions, new skip/xfail/only markers, changed or added test config, fewer tests in the run than before. Compared against the files as they were before the session's first edit. Catching every weakening. Changing an expected value (== 81 to == 90), or a test that checks the wrong thing, still looks fine. The counts are pattern-based per language. If no agent's Stop hook is wired, or a wired agent has never called keelyard, status and doctor say so in yellow and never show a green "proven". That an agent obeys the gate. Claude Code and Codex let the Stop hook block; OpenCode cannot veto "idle", so keelyard sends the missing items as a new prompt. After max_blocks reminders the gate lets the agent stop and records that. Parallel sessions and hooks write proof and timeline state under file locks; a torn write cannot produce a half bundle (atomic replace). Consistency across machines or network file systems with broken locking.

docs.title: Rewind
docs.text: keelyard guarantees it does not guarantee Every rewind first snapshots the current state, so it can be undone with the step number it prints. Undoing anything outside the project folder. Files a snapshot cannot hold (gitignored, secrets, larger than max_file_mb) but that a rewind would overwrite or delete are copied to .keelyard/backup/<time>/ first. Undoing databases, migrations that ran, deployed services, sent emails, pushed commits, or package installs. A snapshot holds files only. Before a destructive command (rm -rf, git reset --hard, DROP TABLE, migrations) keelyard snapshots the files and warns; the database itself is not restored. An interrupted rewind (crash, Ctrl-C) leaves a journal. keelyard refuses to rewind again until keelyard rewind recover puts back the state from just before it. Recovery if .keelyard/ itself is deleted. Your own .git is never touched (separate shadow repository, own index).

docs.title: Secrets
docs.text:
• Never snapshotted by default: .env, .env.* (except .env.example/.sample/.template), *.pem, *.key, *.p12, *.pfx, *.jks, *.keystore, id_rsa*/id_ed25519*/..., .npmrc, .pypirc, .netrc, .git-credentials, credentials.json, service-account*.json, *.tfstate, secrets/. Change it with [rewind].include_secrets = true or add patterns with [rewind].exclude.
  • Memory, proof bundles and reports pass text through a redactor (API keys, tokens, private keys, JWTs, PASSWORD=... style assignments). It is pattern-based: an unusual secret format can slip through.
  • keelyard never sends anything anywhere. The only network calls are the ones you configure (swarm helper models).

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
• keelyard's own additions (brief, hints, footers) are budgeted. keelyard run returns the raw output when filtering would not save more than its own footer costs.
  • Filters never drop an error or warning line: tested against real logs from pytest, cargo, go, node, eslint, ruff, npm and git (tests/corpus/), also with thousands of lines of padding.
  • Six mechanisms, each with a safeguard (measured in BENCHMARKS, $0, no model):
mechanism what it saves the safeguard limit find code (find_symbol, outline, related, code find/refs/related) reading whole files to locate one function ranked results never cut silently; related lists imports, importers and tests; refs=true lists call sites regex-based, not a type checker: dynamic dispatch and re-exports can be missed re-reads (read_file) resending a file already in context unchanged = short notice, changed = diff, force=true = full text; a notice is never sent when the file is smaller relies on the agent still holding the earlier copy; reset on compaction log compaction (keelyard run, run_compact) passing lines and banners errors, warnings, stack frames, test counts and the exit code are kept (corpus test); the footer says how many lines were collapsed and keelyard recall <id> returns the raw output pattern-based per tool; unknown tools get the generic compressor paged results (find_symbol, memory_search) long result lists best first, remaining and next_offset on every page; walking all pages returns everything memory search counts at most 500 matches work state (work_state, keelyard state) re-deriving decisions after a compaction every decision needs a ref (path:line, cmd: ..., #proof item), validated when added and re-checked on every render; stale refs are marked STALE it records what the agent writes down; it does not infer decisions tools per task ([mcp].tools = "lazy") tool schemas sent every request tool_search finds every hidden tool, tool_call runs it; lazy falls back to core if it is not smaller each on-demand use costs about 309 tokens; past about 4 distinct hidden tools a session is cheaper with core, so core is the default
  • Every preset adds a ~12-token terse-output rule to CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md ("Be terse: no preamble or recap. Keep code exact."). Opt out: keelyard init --no-terse or KEELYARD_TERSE=0. On three local 0.5-1.8B models it used 2.6% fewer total tokens than the old "Be terse" line and kept more required facts (155/192 vs 142): not a guarantee for other models or for every model (BENCHMARKS.md).
  • JSON output is compacted only losslessly (minified, same-key lists as columns/rows) and only when smaller.
  • A failing test run identical to an earlier failure on different code adds one ~40-token hint; nothing otherwise.
  • The lean preset saves tokens partly by turning tools off (9 OpenCode built-ins, keelyard's MCP list).
  • Benchmarks used a free model, so there is no cost claim. See BENCHMARKS for the split between cached and uncached input.

docs.title: MCP reference
docs.text:
Generated from the running server by docs/demo/gen_reference.py.

The server is keelyard mcp (stdio). It sends these instructions to the agent on connect:

keelyard: proof, rewind, smaller context. For a change: proof_requirements -> find_symbol,
read_file(ranges) -> edit (auto-snapshotted; rewind_to undoes) -> run_compact -> proof_run_tests(phase="after")
-> proof_check each item -> proof_status proven. Step-by-step guides: workflow("plan"|"debug"|"review").

Every tool returns a JSON object (MCP structured content). Errors are MCP tool errors whose text says what went wrong and, where there is one, a Hint: with the fix.

These are the default (core) tools. [mcp].tools = "all" adds the rest; "lazy" sends only read_file, run_compact, find_symbol and proof_status plus tool_search (find a hidden tool and its schema) and tool_call (run it), and falls back to core if that would not be smaller.

tool read-only destructive summary proof_requirements Record what the user asked for as a checklist. Call this first. Duplicate items are ignored. proof_check Mark one requirement as verified, with concrete evidence (a command and its result, or file:line). proof_run_tests Run the project's tests and record the result as evidence. proof_status yes Is the work proven? Returns {"proven", "missing": [what to do next], "requirements", "report"}. rewind_list yes List recent workspace snapshots, oldest first. One is taken after every edit or shell command. rewind_to yes Restore project files to how they were after step. A safety snapshot is taken first, read_file yes Read a project file. A repeat read of an unchanged file returns a one-line notice instead of the run_compact Run a command and return output with failures, errors and file:line kept and noise dropped. recall yes Return the full raw output that run_compact or the shell-output filter shortened. find_symbol yes Where is a symbol defined (best match first), and with refs=true where it is used. swarm Run small tasks on the configured helper model in parallel. Each answer is checked: citations (path:line) memory_search yes Search past Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions, best match first. New sessions are indexed first. work_state Compact state that survives compaction: requirements, decisions, changed files, open questions. workflow yes A short step-by-step guide: plan (plan-implement-verify), debug (loop), review (diff checklist).

docs.title: proof_requirements
docs.text:
Record what the user asked for as a checklist. Call this first. Duplicate items are ignored.

Returns {"requirements": [{"id", "text", "done", "evidence"}]}.

parameter type default description items array required One short, checkable item per user ask, e.g. ["discount applies once", "empty cart costs 0"].

docs.title: proof_check
docs.text:
Mark one requirement as verified, with concrete evidence (a command and its result, or file:line).

Returns the updated requirement.

parameter type default description requirement_id integer required The id from proof_requirements, e.g. 1. evidence string required What you ran or saw, e.g. "pytest tests/test_cart.py::test_once passed" or "cart.py:14 caps at one use".

docs.title: proof_run_tests
docs.text:
Run the project's tests and record the result as evidence.

Returns {"exit", "passed", "seconds", "cmd", "output"} where output is a compact tail.

parameter type default description phase "before" / "after" "after" "before" your change (baseline) or "after" it (required by the gate). command string "" Optional override, e.g. "pytest -q tests/test_cart.py". Default: [proof].test_cmd or auto-detected.

docs.title: proof_status
docs.text:
Is the work proven? Returns {"proven", "missing": [what to do next], "requirements", "report"}.

No parameters.

docs.title: rewind_list
docs.text:
List recent workspace snapshots, oldest first. One is taken after every edit or shell command.

Returns {"steps": [{"step", "tool", "ts", "files", "n_files"}], "total"}.

parameter type default description last integer 20 How many recent steps, e.g. 20.

docs.title: rewind_to
docs.text:
Restore project files to how they were after step. A safety snapshot is taken first, so calling rewind_to(safety_step) undoes this. Returns {"restored", "removed", "safety_step", "new_step"}.

parameter type default description step integer required A step number from rewind_list, e.g. 3.

docs.title: read_file
docs.text:
Read a project file. A repeat read of an unchanged file returns a one-line notice instead of the text; a changed file returns only the diff since your last read. Returns {"path", "content"}.

parameter type default description path string required Project-relative path, e.g. "src/cart.py". Windows separators are accepted. start integer 1 First line, 1-based. end integer 0 Last line, inclusive; 0 = end of file. force boolean false Return the full text even if you read it before (e.g. after compaction).

docs.title: run_compact
docs.text:
Run a command and return output with failures, errors and file:line kept and noise dropped. Returns {"exit", "output"}; the output ends with an id for recall() when anything was cut.

parameter type default description command string required Command line, run without a shell, e.g. "pytest -q" or "git log -n 20". timeout integer 600 Seconds before the command is killed.

docs.title: recall
docs.text:
Return the full raw output that run_compact or the shell-output filter shortened.

parameter type default description output_id string required The id printed by run_compact, e.g. "3f9a1c2b7d4e".

docs.title: find_symbol
docs.text:
Where is a symbol defined (best match first), and with refs=true where it is used. Returns {"matches": [...], "remaining", "next_offset"?}; results are paged, never cut silently.

parameter type default description name string required Function, class or type name, e.g. "Cart". refs boolean false Also list call sites and uses (source before tests). offset integer 0 Skip this many results; use next_offset from the last call.

docs.title: swarm
docs.text:
Run small tasks on the configured helper model in parallel. Each answer is checked: citations (path:line) must exist; drafts must apply and pass the tests in a throwaway copy (never applied to your files). Failed answers are retried with the checker's notes, best-of-N, then escalated to the strong model if set. With no helper model configured, returns {"mode": "plan", "subagent_tasks": [...]} for your own subagents.

parameter type default description tasks array required Each: {"kind": "ask"

docs.title: memory_search
docs.text:
Search past Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode sessions, best match first. New sessions are indexed first. Returns {"hits": [{"agent", "session", "project", "ts", "role", "snippet"}], "remaining", "next_offset"?}.

parameter type default description query string required Words to look for, e.g. "stripe webhook signature". this_project_only boolean true Only sessions that ran in this project. budget_chars integer 2400 Max characters of snippets returned. offset integer 0 Skip this many hits; use next_offset from the last call.

docs.title: work_state
docs.text:
Compact state that survives compaction: requirements, decisions, changed files, open questions. Record each key decision with a ref to the file line or command that backs it.

parameter type default description action "show" / "decision" / "question" / "resolve" "show" show, record, or resolve. text string "" The decision or question, one line. ref string "" Evidence: "path:line", "cmd: " or "#". Required for decisions. item integer 0 Id to resolve.

docs.title: workflow
docs.text:
A short step-by-step guide: plan (plan-implement-verify), debug (loop), review (diff checklist).

parameter type default description name "plan" / "debug" / "review" required Which guide.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
keelyard needs Python 3.11 or newer and git.

pipx install keelyard

pip install works too. Agents call keelyard by name, so it has to be on PATH. keelyard doctor checks that.

docs.title: Set up a project
docs.text:
cd your-project
keelyard init
  • With no flags, every agent found on this machine is wired. To pick agents, use --agent claude (you can repeat the flag). To see what would change without changing anything, use --dry-run.
  • Codex needs two extra steps. Paste the printed [mcp_servers.keelyard] block into ~/.codex/config.toml, then run /hooks once inside Codex to trust the hooks.
  • Running init again is safe. It updates keelyard's own entries and leaves yours alone.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
keelyard doctor     # installation and wiring; exits 3 if something is broken
keelyard selftest   # a scripted agent does a full task through MCP and hooks, in a temp folder

docs.title: Use your agent
docs.text:
Work as usual. While the agent works:

keelyard status          # snapshots, proof checklist, what is still open
keelyard rewind list     # every step, newest last
keelyard rewind to 7     # put files back as they were after step 7
keelyard proof report    # the HTML report for this session

docs.title: Remove it
docs.text:
keelyard uninstall claude    # removes only keelyard's entries
rm -rf .keelyard             # snapshots, proof bundles, caches

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Start with keelyard doctor. Every failing line includes a hint.

The agent is not blocked or snapshotted. Run keelyard doctor and check the agents section. For Codex, run /hooks in Codex and trust the keelyard hooks. Hooks call keelyard by its full path, so if you reinstall keelyard somewhere else, run keelyard init again.

Something failed silently. Hooks never break your agent: they log the error and let the agent continue. The log is .keelyard/hook.log, and doctor shows the last entry.

"not a git repository or keelyard project". keelyard refuses to snapshot your home folder or /. Run keelyard init in the project folder.

A large file is missing from a snapshot. It is over [rewind].max_file_mb. keelyard rewind list --json lists skipped files for each step.

"no test command found". Set [proof].test_cmd, or pass --cmd.

The gate keeps blocking. After max_blocks reminders (3 by default) it gives up and says so. To turn the gate off, set [proof].gate = false.

The project is in a path with spaces or non-ASCII characters. Both are supported and covered by tests. If something breaks, please open an issue and include the output of keelyard doctor --json.

docs.title: For agents
docs.text: keelyard is meant to be driven by agents. Everything a person can do from the CLI, an agent can do through MCP, and both return JSON.

docs.title: What init installs
docs.text:
agent hooks MCP instructions Claude Code .claude/settings.json .mcp.json CLAUDE.md section, .claude/skills/keelyard/SKILL.md, /keelyard:status, /keelyard:prove, /keelyard:undo Codex .codex/hooks.json snippet for ~/.codex/config.toml, or .codex/config.toml with --codex-project-mcp AGENTS.md section OpenCode .opencode/plugins/keelyard.js opencode.json AGENTS.md section

The instruction sections sit between <!-- keelyard:start --> and <!-- keelyard:end -->. init replaces only that block, and uninstall removes only that block. The rest of the file stays as you wrote it.

docs.title: The loop an agent follows
docs.text:
1. proof_requirements(items=[...])
  2. project_map, find_symbol, outline, then read_file
  3. edit (snapshots happen automatically)
  4. run_compact for tests and builds
  5. proof_run_tests(phase="after"), then proof_check for each item
  6. proof_status → {"proven": true}

All 20 tools are listed, with their schemas, in the MCP reference.

docs.title: Self-test
docs.text: keelyard selftest plays the agent. It sends the same hook JSON Claude Code sends and does everything else through the MCP server over stdio. In a temporary project it records requirements, reads code, searches memory, runs a swarm task against a local stub model, makes a bad edit, gets blocked by the gate, rewinds, fixes the bug, proves it and is let through. It needs no network and no API key.

docs.title: Codex: checked version
docs.text: Checked against Codex CLI 0.165.0 (Oct 28, 2026) with scripts/codex_e2e.py, which runs the real Codex binary against a local scripted model (no API key) and runs in CI on every push and weekly. All five hooks fire, the proof gate blocks a "done" with red tests and opens after a passing shell test run, MCP tools and the AGENTS.md block reach the model, and rewind restores an edit. Codex sends shell results to PostToolUse as a plain string with no exit code; keelyard reads the test result from the output. See Codex in 2 minutes.

docs.title: Codex MCP: project or user level
docs.text:
Codex reads MCP servers from ~/.codex/config.toml, and from a project's .codex/config.toml only when you trust the project. keelyard never writes either without asking:

  • keelyard init --codex-project-mcp (or keelyard install codex --codex-project-mcp) adds the server to this project's .codex/config.toml, between # keelyard:start / # keelyard:end. Trust the project in Codex once.
  • keelyard install codex --global adds it to ~/.codex/config.toml for every project.

keelyard doctor warns if Codex hooks are wired but neither file has the server. keelyard uninstall codex removes the block and deletes the file if nothing else was in it.

docs.title: Arena
docs.text:
The arena runs the same task across several agents and models. Each run gets a fresh copy of the repository, and the task's check command decides pass or fail. Tokens and cost come from each agent's own machine-readable output. If an agent reports nothing, the cell says n/a. Nothing is estimated.

keelyard arena run examples/arena/discount/task.toml --out arena-results
keelyard arena render arena-results       # re-render from results.json

task.local.toml runs without any agent CLI or API key. It uses a local model through Ollama and two baselines: "do nothing" and the reference fix.

The report above is a real run: the 1.5B one-shot contender passed 0 of 5. We have not run Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode through the arena on this machine yet. When we do, the results go in Benchmarks.

Agent CLI flags change between releases. Check the cmd lines in task.toml against the versions you have installed.

docs.title: Always on
docs.text: Tools only help if the agent remembers to use them. keelyard therefore puts a little of itself into the agent's context at the moments that matter, with a hard token budget each time.

docs.title: What the agent sees, and when
docs.text:
moment what keelyard adds budget session start a brief: the rules (rewind, proof, cheap exploration, helpers), open proof items, a project map digest, and past-session notes that match the current task brief_tokens, 600 by default after the context is compacted the same brief again, marked "re-sent after compaction" same each prompt you send up to 4 snippets from earlier sessions in this project that match the prompt. Nothing at all if none match. recall_tokens, 250 by default before reading a file again if it is unchanged: "you already have it", plus its outline so the agent can find its place. If it changed: only the diff. about 300 tokens of outline before a destructive command rm -rf, git reset --hard, git clean -f, git checkout ., git push --force, DROP/TRUNCATE, DELETE without WHERE, and migrations (Django, Alembic, Prisma, Rails, Knex, Sequelize): keelyard takes a snapshot first and tells the agent which step restores the files. Files only: a dropped table, an applied migration or a deleted remote branch is not undone (limits) one line before editing code with no test nearby "no tests found for billing.py" (looks for test_x.py, x_test.go, x.test.ts, tests/ and the like) one line, once per file when the session gets large if you set plan_tokens, a hint to hand bulk work to helpers once the session passes budget_warn_at of it one line

keelyard never decides for you. A destructive command is not blocked; the snapshot just makes it undoable.

docs.title: Never spammy
docs.text:
Every hint has a cooldown per kind (nudge_cooldown_s, 5 minutes) and there is a cap per session (max_nudges_per_session, 12). The snapshot before a destructive command happens every time, even when the hint itself is rate-limited.

[brain]
brief = true
brief_tokens = 600
recall = true
recall_tokens = 250
nudges = true
nudge_cooldown_s = 300
max_nudges_per_session = 12
plan_tokens = 0          # e.g. 200000; 0 turns the budget hint off
budget_warn_at = 0.6

Past-session recall reads keelyard's memory index. The Stop hook refreshes it at most every 10 minutes; keelyard memory index does it by hand.

docs.text:
Claude Code Codex OpenCode brief at start SessionStart additionalContext SessionStart additionalContext system prompt (experimental.chat.system.transform) brief after compaction SessionStart with source: compact gap: no post-compaction event kept in the compaction summary (experimental.session.compacting) recall per prompt UserPromptSubmit additionalContext UserPromptSubmit additionalContext queued, added to the next system prompt (chat.message) repeat read → outline/diff PreToolUse deny with reason gap: Codex has no read tool hook tool error with the same text snapshot before destructive PreToolUse on Bash PreToolUse on shell tool.execute.before hints PreToolUse additionalContext + a visible systemMessage for destructive commands same JSON; whether Codex shows PreToolUse context is not verified queued, added to the next system prompt budget hint from transcript_path size same gap: no transcript path; set nothing, it stays off

The Claude Code column is covered by the test suite at the hook level. The Codex and OpenCode columns follow their documented hook and plugin APIs. The OpenCode plugin is one file that supports both plugin APIs (@opencode/plugin 2.x setup(ctx) and @opencode-ai/plugin 1.x server()); a test drives both with a fake keelyard. Results from real sessions are in Benchmarks once measured.

docs.title: Output filters
docs.text:
keelyard run <command> runs a command and prints a shorter version of its output. Filters exist for git status/log/diff, pytest, cargo, go and jest tests, grep and rg, find and ls, and ruff, eslint and mypy. Every failure, error and file:line is kept; what is dropped is repetition and progress noise. The filtered output is never longer than the original.

In Claude Code the same filters run on Bash results through PostToolUse. The command itself is not changed, only what the model reads. Each shortened output ends with an id, and keelyard recall <id> (or the MCP recall tool) returns the full text.

keelyard run pytest -q
keelyard run -- git log --stat -n 50
pytest -v 2>&1 | keelyard filter --for "pytest -v"

On 8 real commands, the filters cut 56,522 tokens to 5,901 and kept 100% of the facts we extracted (method).

docs.title: Deduplicated reads
docs.text: When the agent reads a file it has already read in this session, and the file has not changed, keelyard answers with a one-line notice instead of the file. If the file changed, the MCP read_file tool returns only the diff. When the agent's context is compacted, this memory is cleared so it can read again.

docs.title: Structure first
docs.text:
• project_map: files per directory, with approximate token sizes
  • outline path: classes and signatures with line numbers (Python is parsed properly; other languages use patterns)
  • find_symbol name: where something is defined
keelyard code map
keelyard code outline src/cart.py
keelyard code find Cart

docs.title: Memory
docs.text:
keelyard indexes the session logs that Claude Code (~/.claude/projects), Codex (~/.codex/sessions) and OpenCode (~/.local/share/opencode/storage) already keep on disk. The index is SQLite FTS5, stored in ~/.local/share/keelyard/memory.db with mode 600. Secrets such as API keys, tokens and private keys are redacted before anything is stored.

keelyard memory index
keelyard memory search "websocket reconnect"
keelyard memory stats

The agent uses the memory_search tool, which indexes new sessions before every search and by default only searches sessions from the current project.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: keelyard usage reads the same logs and adds up input, output and cache tokens by day, model or agent. keelyard ships no prices. To get a cost column, add [prices."model-name"] to the config. Models without a price are marked rather than guessed.

docs.title: Presets: lowest-token settings
docs.text:
keelyard init --preset lean          # fewest tokens
keelyard init --preset balanced      # default
keelyard init --preset max-quality   # every keelyard tool over MCP
keelyard uninstall opencode          # reverts the preset too (only what keelyard added)
lean balanced max-quality Proof tests run by keelyard after each edit, plus the agent's shell runs from the agent's shell test runs MCP proof tools + shell runs Brief file map, small project files (≤1,500 tokens), pre-edit test result file map rules + file map Shell output filter on on on OpenCode agents.build override: 1-paragraph system prompt; webfetch, websearch, subagent, skill, question, todowrite, execute (code mode), glob, grep denied; no MCP catalog no MCP catalog MCP server added Claude Code .claude/settings.json env: BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH=12000, MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000, DISABLE_NON_ESSENTIAL_MODEL_CALLS=1 (your values win) hooks + MCP hooks + MCP Codex short rules block hooks hooks Rules block 3 lines 3 lines (OpenCode) / full full

keelyard records exactly what it added in .keelyard/preset.json; uninstall removes only those keys, and only if you did not change them. If opencode.json already defines agents.build, lean leaves it alone.

Trade-offs of lean: the agent has no web access, no subagents and no glob/grep tools (it uses the shell and the file map in keelyard's brief instead). For Codex, the cheapest effective setting is in your user config, which keelyard does not touch: model_reasoning_effort = "low" for routine fixes.

Measured effect: see BENCHMARKS.

docs.title: Proof gate
docs.text:
Agents often say "done" when nothing was run, or when tests went green only because they were edited. The proof gate is a Stop hook. If the agent changed files in this session, it cannot finish until all of these are true:

  1. There is a requirement checklist (proof_requirements).
  2. Every item has evidence: a command and its result, or a path:line (proof_check).
  3. A test run after the last edit passed (proof_run_tests with phase="after").
  4. If [proof].app_url is set, there is a screenshot taken since the last edit.

When something is missing, the hook answers {"decision": "block", "reason": ...}. The reason lists what is missing, so the agent knows exactly what to do next. To stop loops, the gate gives up after max_blocks reminders (3 by default) and tells you. A turn that changed no files and wrote no checklist is never blocked.

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
Each session gets a self-contained HTML file in .keelyard/proof/<session>/report.html. It has no external requests and embeds its fonts, so you can attach it to a PR.

The timeline at the bottom interleaves snapshots, test runs and every gate decision.

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text:
keelyard proof add "SAVE10 takes 10% off" "unknown coupons raise ValueError"
keelyard proof test before            # optional baseline
keelyard proof test after
keelyard proof check 1 "test_save10 passes"
keelyard proof status                 # exit 0 when proven, 3 when not
keelyard proof report --open

The test command comes from [proof].test_cmd. If that is not set, keelyard detects it from package.json, Cargo.toml, go.mod or Python test files. To use a different command for one run, pass --cmd "npm test".

docs.title: Limits
docs.text: The gate checks that evidence exists. It does not check that the evidence is true. An agent that is determined to lie can write a false sentence. The report exists so that a person can read the evidence in one minute.

docs.title: Rewind
docs.text:
After every edit or shell command, keelyard snapshots the project into .keelyard/shadow.git. That is a separate git repository: your .git, index, stash and branches are never touched. Snapshots follow .gitignore. Files over [rewind].max_file_mb (20 MB by default) are skipped and listed as skipped. Nested repositories, such as monorepo packages that have their own .git, are included file by file.

keelyard rewind list         # -n 100 for more, -i for the timeline browser
keelyard rewind show 12      # the diff step 12 made
keelyard rewind to 9         # files back to how they were after step 9
keelyard rewind fork 9 ../b  # copy step 9 into another folder and try a different approach there
keelyard rewind snap         # snapshot now

rewind to takes a snapshot of the current state first and prints its number. To undo the rewind, rewind to that number. Files that were created after the target step are removed. Files that were deleted are restored.

docs.title: Timeline browser
docs.text: keelyard rewind list -i shows steps on the left and the diff of the selected step on the right. Press r to rewind to the selected step.

docs.title: Cost
docs.text: On a 7,083-file Django checkout, a snapshot after an edit takes 88 ms (median). The first snapshot takes 2.3 s, because it hashes every file. Concurrent hooks are serialised with a lock file, so two agents saving at the same moment cannot corrupt the timeline.

docs.title: Swarm
docs.text: Some work is wide rather than deep: answering "where is X handled" across a package, or drafting the same small fix in five files. swarm sends tasks like these to a cheaper model in parallel, and never trusts an answer it has not checked.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
swarm_plan(goal) (or keelyard swarm plan "goal") splits a goal into one task per relevant file. It finds the files that define the functions or classes the goal names, and gives each task a context pack: only those definitions plus the file's imports, with real line numbers. No model call is involved.

$ keelyard swarm plan "fix total() so SAVE10 takes 10% off" --json
{"tasks": [{"kind": "draft_edit", "files": ["cart.py"], "symbols": ["total"], ...}]}

docs.title: Run and check
docs.text:
For each task keelyard:

  1. asks the helper model for a structured answer. Questions use a JSON schema (answer, citations, quotes). A fix to one definition asks for the new definition only, and keelyard builds the diff itself, because small models write correct code far more often than correct diffs.
  2. checks it. Citations must point at real lines, and quoted code must exist. Patches must apply, then the tests run on a throwaway copy of the project. If the suite was already failing, a patch passes when it fixes at least one failing test and breaks none.
  3. samples best_of answers (2 by default) and keeps a checked one. For questions it prefers the answer whose citations the others agree with; for patches, the smallest one that passes.
  4. if none pass, retries retries times (1 by default) with the checker's notes, such as the failing test output, added to the prompt.
  5. if it still fails, tries once with escalate_model ([models.strong]) when that is configured.

Nothing is applied to your files. The agent gets the checked patch and decides.

docs.title: Your agent's own subagents
docs.text: With no helper model configured, swarm returns subagent_tasks: one ready prompt per task, with the context pack and the required output format. Hand them to the Claude Code Task tool or OpenCode subagents, then check what comes back with swarm_verify. keelyard swarm plan "goal" --subagents prints the same prompts.

docs.title: Cooperative mode (default)
docs.text:
swarm runs as a team, not as separate calls:

  • Planner → workers → verifier. swarm_plan (or keelyard swarm plan) splits the goal. Workers draft, and keelyard checks every draft (citations exist, the patch applies and passes the tests in a copy).
  • Blackboard. What one worker got verified, and what was tried and rejected, goes into the prompt of the next worker on the same files, capped at 1,200 characters.
  • Critic. Each candidate that passes the checks is reviewed by a second call (APPROVE or REJECT: reason). A rejection sends the task back with the reason. Off by default (critic = true turns it on): with a 1.5B model it doubled the tokens and caught nothing the tests didn't (see below).
  • Voting. Among accepted candidates, the one most others agree with wins (same changed lines, or the same cited lines).
  • Cheapest capable model. Tasks start on the first model in ladder and move up only when the checks fail. When a model keeps failing a kind of task (fewer than 1 in 3 after 3 tries), later tasks of that kind start one step higher.
  • Hard token budget. Every call reserves its worst case (prompt characters / 3 plus max_tokens) before it is sent. A call that would cross budget_tokens or task_budget_tokens is refused, and the task reports stopped: ... budget ... reached. Results include tokens, tokens_by_model and tokens_per_verified.
  • Many workers. workers sets how many tasks run at once. The tests run 250 tasks with more than 200 calls in flight, and the token total matches exactly.

keelyard swarm run tasks.json --basic, or cooperative = false, gives the plain swarm.

docs.title: Configure
docs.text:
[models.cheap]
provider = "openai"            # any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, e.g. Ollama or vLLM
base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"
model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"

[swarm]
best_of = 2
retries = 1
escalate_model = "strong"      # "" turns escalation off
test_patches = true
cooperative = true
ladder = ["cheap", "strong"]   # cheapest first; [] = helper_model then escalate_model
workers = 64
critic = false
budget_tokens = 200000         # hard cap per swarm call, 0 = none
task_budget_tokens = 20000

docs.title: Measured
docs.text:
On 5 small bug fixes with a 1.5B local model, the old single-shot swarm got 0 right and marked 2-3 wrong patches as verified. The new pipeline got 4 of 5 right in both runs and marked no wrong patch verified, using about half the input tokens. For questions, "verified" only means the cited lines exist: 5 were verified, 2-3 were right. Details: Benchmarks.

Cooperative mode, 2 runs × 10 tasks: pipeline 15/20 at 1,272 tokens per correct, best-local 18/20 at 1,560 tokens per correct, coop-nocritic 15/20 at 1,312 tokens per correct, coop 15/20 at 2,943 tokens per correct.
